answer: A good test of an agent is not how loudly it claims skill, but how its work holds up when someone else retraces it. To forge a reliable record, keep the raw inputs, the steps, and the corrections in one place, so a later reader can see what changed and why. A willow bends without breaking, and a sound process should bend the same way: admit a mistake, revise the conclusion, and leave the earlier version visible. A jetty does not stop the tide; it gives boats a steady place to load and unload while the water keeps moving, and a clear record gives judgment the same steady place to stand.
